samples.summary: No test asserts a supplied `parentId` is actually passed through to `folderService.create`
samples.evidence: `create` has three happy-path tests: line 86 asserts the default `parentId: null`, line 96 asserts only that `assertSameWorkspace` was called with ('f-9', WS), and line 114 asserts only `objectContaining({ authorID })`. The new rejection test (line 104) asserts `create` was NOT called. So if `folders.controller.ts:100` were changed to always pass `parentId: null` (dropping `body.parentId ?? null`), every create test would still pass while every API-created subfolder silently landed at the workspace root — a user-visible misfiling with no coverage. The delta added a create test but did not close this pass-through gap.

samples.evidence: The header comment (lines 11-16) states `list` and `create` "trust the route `workspaceId` outright" and that dropping `WorkspaceScopeGuard` lets a key minted for one workspace read/write another — then covers that only by asserting guard *metadata* (`Reflect.getMetadata('__guards__')`, line 29) and relative ordering (line 36). finding.summary: `create`'s cross-workspace parent check is only asserted by "the mock was called" — no test proves a rejected parent stops the folder being created
finding.evidence: The only coverage for the parent check in `create` is `it('checks a supplied parent belongs to the route workspace')`, which asserts `expect(folderService.assertSameWorkspace).toHaveBeenCalledWith('f-9', WS)` and nothing else. That assertion holds even if the controller dropped the `await` (or ignored a rejection), in which case a folder could be parented under a folder in another workspace. The sibling `documents.controller.spec.ts` does have the corresponding negative case ('refuses a folder from another workspace' → rejects and `updateDocument` not called); the folders spec has no equivalent for `create`: no test mocks `assertSameWorkspace.mockRejectedValue(...)` and asserts `folderService.create` was not called. The v1 folders routes also have no e2e coverage (packages/backend/test/folder.e2e-spec.ts only hits the web routes `/workspaces/:id/folders` and `/folders/:id`), so nothing else exercises this path.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test proves a rejected cross-workspace parent stops folder creation, and specifically that "no test mocks assertSameWorkspace.mockRejectedValue(...) and asserts folderService.create was not called". That test exists verbatim: folders.controller.spec.ts:104-112, `it('creates nothing when the parent is in another workspace')`, inside the same describe('create') block immediately below the test the finding quotes as the "only coverage". It mocks assertSameWorkspace.mockRejectedValue(new BadRequestException(...)), asserts controller.create rejects with BadRequestException, and asserts folderService.create was not called. It also directly defeats the named failure mode: if the `await` at folders.controller.ts:95 were dropped, execution would continue to folderService.create and both assertions would fail — the test's own preceding comment states this rationale. The equivalent negative case for `update` also exists at lines 218-227. Since the behavior is meaningfully covered at the unit level, the noted lack of v1 e2e coverage does not sustain the finding.
